# BH-700 Kiln Baghouse: Control Narrative (Draft A)

**Source:** Shift supervisor email (Dave). Values marked *email* come from that email. They need confirmation before they go into the setpoint list.

**Status:** Draft for operations and process review. It is not ready for issue. Section 10 lists the items that block programming.

---

## 1. Purpose and Boundaries

BH-700 removes particulate from the kiln exhaust gas. It discharges the collected dust through RV-702 to SC-701.

| Interface | Direction | Connected module | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Kiln exhaust gas | In, through D-704 | Kiln | TT-705 measures inlet temperature |
| Bleed air | In, through D-706 | Atmosphere | Used for temperature protection |
| Clean gas | Out, through F-703 | Stack | — |
| Dust | Out, RV-702 to SC-701 | Dust handling (downstream of SC-701, TBD) | OI-09 |
| Kiln feed stop / permissive | Out | Kiln feed module | Defined in the C&E chart |

---

## 2. Equipment and Tags

Refer to the instrument index for ranges, I/O, and fail positions. The email does not name the tags marked *TBD*. These are required for this narrative (OI-03).

| Tag | Function |
|---|---|
| SC-701 | Dust screw conveyor (downstream of RV-702) |
| RV-702 | Hopper rotary airlock |
| SSL-7xx (TBD) | RV-702 motion (zero-speed) switch |
| F-703 | ID fan |
| D-704, ZSO/ZSC-704 (TBD) | Inlet damper and position switches |
| D-706, ZSO/ZSC-706 (TBD) | Bleed-air damper and position switches |
| TT-705 | Baghouse inlet temperature |
| PDT-7xx (TBD) | Tube-sheet differential pressure |
| LSH-7xx (TBD) | Hopper high level |
| Pulse controller (TBD) | Row solenoid valves |

---

## 3. Setpoint List (Single Source of Truth)

All numbers in this narrative are in this list. Prose and tables refer to the SP-ID only.

| SP-ID | Parameter | Value | Source / status |
|---|---|---|---|
| SP-01 | Delay from F-703 running to D-704 open command | 60 s | Email ("a minute or so"). Confirm. |
| SP-02 | Normal pulse interval, per row | 10 s | Email |
| SP-03 | High-rate pulse interval, per row | 5 s | Email |
| SP-04 | DP high: change to high rate | 6 inWC | Email ("6 or 7"). Confirm. |
| SP-05 | DP reset: return to normal rate | TBD | Not in email. Must be below SP-04. |
| SP-06 | DP high-high: kiln feed stop | 8 inWC | Email |
| SP-07 | Clean-down duration | 10 min | Email |
| SP-08 | TT-705 high: open D-706 | 450 °F | Email. Check against bag rating (OI-06). |
| SP-09 | TT-705 reset: close D-706 | TBD | Not in email. Must be below SP-08. |
| SP-10 | TT-705 high-high action limit | TBD | Not in email (OI-06) |
| SP-11 | Motor run-feedback timeout (SC-701, RV-702, F-703) | TBD | Not in email |
| SP-12 | Damper travel timeout (D-704, D-706) | TBD | Vendor data |
| SP-13 | RV-702 motion-loss confirmation delay | TBD | Not in email |
| SP-14 | Hopper empty-out run time after F-703 stop | TBD | Not in email (OI-08) |

---

## 4. States and Transitions (ISA-106)

Use state-based control for the BH-700 unit. Use sequence-based control for the start and stop jobs in Section 6.

| State | Description | Entry permissives | Allowed exits | Initiator | Automation level |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| STOPPED | All equipment stopped. D-704 closed. | Stop or reset complete | STARTING | Operator | Operator-initiated |
| STARTING | Start sequence (Table 6.1) | All start permissives true (FR-BH700-001) | RUNNING; TRIPPED | Operator / auto at sequence end | Automatic after START |
| RUNNING | Gas flow through bags. Pulse cleaning active. | Start sequence complete | CLEAN-DOWN; TRIPPED | Operator / auto | Automatic |
| CLEAN-DOWN | Normal stop with cleaning (Table 6.2) | Kiln feed stopped (FR-BH700-020) | STOPPED; TRIPPED | Operator / auto at sequence end | Operator-prompted, then automatic |
| TRIPPED | Fast stop on a C&E trip cause (Table 6.3) | Any trip cause in C&E chart | STOPPED (after reset) | Auto / operator | Automatic entry. Operator reset. |

**Not allowed:** a direct transition from STOPPED to RUNNING; a direct transition from TRIPPED to STARTING; automatic restart from any state.

---

## 5. Regulatory and Discrete Control

### 5.1 Pulse Cleaning

| ID | Requirement | Test method |
|---|---|---|
| FR-BH700-010 | Pulse one row at a time at the SP-02 interval while BH-700 is in RUNNING or CLEAN-DOWN. | FAT: measure the interval between row outputs. |
| FR-BH700-011 | Change to the SP-03 interval when PDT-7xx is above SP-04. | FAT: simulate DP above SP-04. Measure the interval. |
| FR-BH700-012 | Return to the SP-02 interval when PDT-7xx is below SP-05. | FAT: simulate DP falling below SP-05. |
| FR-BH700-013 | Use the SP-03 interval when PDT-7xx is bad quality. | FAT: force bad quality. |
| FR-BH700-014 | Stop pulsing in STOPPED and TRIPPED. | FAT: verify that no row outputs occur. |

Pulsing starts when D-704 is open. This is a basis assumption. It needs confirmation (OI-07).

### 5.2 Inlet Temperature Protection (D-706)

Basis: on/off control with deadband. This follows the email. Modulating control is an alternative (OI-06).

| ID | Requirement | Test method |
|---|---|---|
| FR-BH700-015 | Open D-706 when TT-705 is above SP-08. | FAT: simulate TT-705. Verify the open command and ZSO-706. |
| FR-BH700-016 | Close D-706 when TT-705 is below SP-09. | FAT: simulate TT-705 falling. |
| FR-BH700-017 | Open D-706 when TT-705 is bad quality. | FAT: force bad quality. |

No tuning values are in this document.

---

## 6. Sequences

### 6.1 Start Sequence (STOPPED → RUNNING)

The sequence starts the discharge path before the fan. SC-701 is downstream of RV-702. If RV-702 runs into a stopped SC-701, the conveyor plugs and the hopper fills. This is the 2019 fire scenario. Mike's fan-first practice is recorded as OI-01.

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Check start permissives (FR-BH700-001). | All permissives true | None. Hold. | Stay in STOPPED. Show the missing permissive. |
| 2 | Start SC-701. | SC-701 run feedback | SP-11 | Go to TRIPPED. Alarm "SC-701 fail to start". |
| 3 | Start RV-702. | RV-702 run feedback and SSL-7xx motion | SP-11 | Go to TRIPPED. Alarm "RV-702 fail to start". |
| 4 | Start F-703. | F-703 run feedback | SP-11 | Go to TRIPPED. Alarm "F-703 fail to start". |
| 5 | Wait SP-01. | Timer complete and F-703 running | SP-01 | If F-703 stops, go to TRIPPED. |
| 6 | Open D-704. | ZSO-704 made | SP-12 | Close D-704. Go to TRIPPED. Alarm "D-704 fail to open". |
| 7 | Start pulse cleaning (FR-BH700-010). | Pulse controller running feedback | SP-11 | Alarm "Pulse fault". Stay in RUNNING (OI-07). |
| 8 | Go to RUNNING. | — | — | — |

| ID | Requirement | Test method |
|---|---|---|
| FR-BH700-001 | Do not start unless: no trip active, D-704 closed, SC-701/RV-702/F-703 in remote and available, LSH-7xx not active. | FAT: remove each permissive one at a time. Verify that START is blocked. |
| FR-BH700-002 | Execute Table 6.1 in step order. | FAT: run the sequence. Record the step times. |
| FR-BH700-003 | Apply the failure response for each step on timeout. | FAT: block each feedback. Verify the response. |

### 6.2 Normal Stop / Clean-Down (RUNNING → CLEAN-DOWN → STOPPED)

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Prompt operator: "Make sure kiln feed is stopped." | Kiln feed stopped signal | None. Hold. | Stay in RUNNING. |
| 2 | Keep F-703, D-704 position, and pulsing. Start SP-07 timer. | Timer complete | SP-07 | On a trip cause, go to TRIPPED. |
| 3 | Stop pulse cleaning. | Pulse stopped | SP-11 | Alarm. Continue. |
| 4 | Close D-704. | ZSC-704 made | SP-12 | Alarm "D-704 fail to close". Continue. |
| 5 | Stop F-703. | F-703 run feedback off | SP-11 | Alarm "F-703 fail to stop". |
| 6 | Run RV-702 and SC-701 for SP-14. | Timer complete | SP-14 | On RV-702 motion loss, alarm. |
| 7 | Stop RV-702, then SC-701. | Run feedback off | SP-11 | Alarm. |
| 8 | Go to STOPPED. | — | — | — |

D-704 position during clean-down is an assumption (OI-08). The email does not say.

| ID | Requirement | Test method |
|---|---|---|
| FR-BH700-020 | Do not enter CLEAN-DOWN until the kiln feed stopped signal is true. | FAT: simulate kiln feed running. Verify a hold at step 1. |
| FR-BH700-021 | Execute Table 6.2 in step order. | FAT: run the sequence. Record the step times. |

### 6.3 Trip (Any State → TRIPPED)

The trip causes and effects are in the C&E chart. Section 7 lists the proposed rows. The sequence executes all effects at the same time, not in steps.

| ID | Requirement | Test method |
|---|---|---|
| FR-BH700-030 | On any BH-700 trip cause, execute all effects in the C&E chart and go to TRIPPED. | FAT: simulate each cause. Verify each effect. |
| FR-BH700-031 | Require operator reset in TRIPPED before START is available. | FAT: verify that START is blocked until reset. |

---

## 7. Interlocks and Permissives

Refer to the BH-700 cause-and-effect chart. The chart does not exist yet. The rows below are **input to the C&E chart**. When they move to the chart, remove them from this narrative.

| Proposed cause | Proposed effect | Email basis | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| RV-702 motion loss for SP-13 | BH-700 TRIPPED. Stop F-703. Close D-704. Stop kiln feed. | "Shut everything down quick... fire in 2019" | Candidate SIF (OI-04). Stopping the fan while the kiln runs has a process consequence (OI-05). |
| SC-701 stopped while RV-702 runs | Stop RV-702, then as above | Implied by the start order | — |
| LSH-7xx active | As for RV-702 motion loss | Not in email | New instrument (OI-03) |
| PDT-7xx above SP-06 | Stop kiln feed | "Over 8 we usually shut the kiln feed" | "Usually" means operator judgment now. Basis here is automatic. Confirm (OI-02). |
| F-703 stopped in RUNNING | BH-700 TRIPPED. Stop kiln feed. | Not in email | — |
| TT-705 above SP-10 | TBD | Not in email | OI-06 |

**SIS:** The 2019 hopper fire shows a hazard that may need an SIF. The PHA/LOPA decides this. If an SIF is assigned, the IEC 61511 SRS specifies it. This narrative then references the SRS and does not take credit for the BPCS trip.

---

## 8. Alarms

Refer to the rationalized alarm database (ISA-18.2). The candidate alarms below need rationalization. Priority and setpoints come from that database.

- PDT-7xx high (SP-04 basis), high-high (SP-06 basis), bad quality
- TT-705 high (SP-08 basis), high-high (SP-10 basis), bad quality
- RV-702 motion loss; LSH-7xx active
- Fail to start, fail to stop, or fail to move for each item in Tables 6.1 and 6.2
- Pulse controller fault; communications loss

---

## 9. Abnormal Handling

| Condition | Required response | ID | Test method |
|---|---|---|---|
| PDT-7xx bad quality | Pulse at the SP-03 interval. Alarm. No kiln feed stop on bad DP alone. | FR-BH700-040 | FAT: force bad quality. |
| TT-705 bad quality | Open D-706. Alarm. | FR-BH700-041 | FAT: force bad quality. |
| SSL-7xx bad / wire break | Treat as motion loss | FR-BH700-042 | FAT: open the circuit. |
| Comms loss to MCC or pulse controller | Alarm. Go to TRIPPED if run status of SC-701, RV-702, or F-703 is lost. | FR-BH700-043 | FAT: disconnect the comms link. |
| Power loss and restart | Go to STOPPED on restore. No automatic restart. | FR-BH700-044 | FAT: cycle the controller power. |
| Fail positions on loss of air/signal | D-704: closed (proposed). D-706: open (proposed). | FR-BH700-045 | FAT: remove air and signal. Record the positions. |

Fail positions are proposed. The instrument index must confirm them (OI-10).

---

## 10. Operator Interface

| ID | Requirement | Test method |
|---|---|---|
| FR-BH700-050 | Show BH-700 state, active sequence step, and step timer on the BH-700 display. | FAT: observe through each state. |
| FR-BH700-051 | Provide START, STOP, and RESET on the BH-700 faceplate. | FAT: operate each command. |
| FR-BH700-052 | Show which start permissive is missing. | FAT: remove each permissive. |
| FR-BH700-053 | Show the pulse rate (normal or high), PDT-7xx, TT-705, and D-706 position. | FAT: observe. |
| FR-BH700-054 | Show the prompt "Make sure kiln feed is stopped." in CLEAN-DOWN step 1. | FAT: observe. |

Operations must sign off on the states in Section 4 and the prompts in this section.

## Traceability: Email to Requirement

| Email statement | Where it went |
|---|---|
| SC-701 and RV-702 first, then F-703 | Table 6.1, steps 2–4; OI-01 |
| "Mike likes to start the fan first... either works" | OI-01 (the system needs one sequence) |
| "Wait a minute or so" before D-704 | SP-01; Table 6.1 step 5 |
| One row every 10 s; every 5 s at "6 or 7 in." | SP-02, SP-03, SP-04; FR-BH700-010/011; OI-02 |
| "Over 8 we usually shut the kiln feed" | SP-06; C&E input row; OI-02 |
| Airlock stops → shut down, 2019 fire | C&E input row; OI-04, OI-05 |
| Pulse 10 min with fan running on shutdown | SP-07; Table 6.2 |
| TT-705 over 450 °F → open D-706 | SP-08; FR-BH700-015; OI-06 |

**For the integrator:** You can program Sections 4–6 and 9 now as a structure. Do not set final values or the C&E logic until OI-01, OI-02, OI-04, and OI-05 are closed. These four items change the trip behavior.
